subject: Latency surge: Hosted API p95/p99 regressions — cache coherency blip
messages:
From: ops@bluewave-analytics.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: URGENT: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on Hosted API

Marissa / Redwood support —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency (~15:15 UTC) on the production Hosted API route that our service calls. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and p99 is spiking to 3–4s. Error rate is also up slightly (5xxs), throughput temporarily stepped up (we had a burst to ~1.6k RPS). This is impacting customer-facing query flows.

Attached is a quick chart of p95/p99 over the last hour and a few trace snippets. Can you confirm if there were any config changes or clear cache events on your side? We reproduce this across two regions (us-east and us-west).

We need a timeline and mitigation ASAP — can you please escalate?

— Alice Chen
CTO, BlueWave Analytics
attachments: p95_p99_graph.png, trace-snippets.txt
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ops@bluewave-analytics.com, alice.chen@bluewave-analytics.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:31:12 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on Hosted API

Alice — thanks for the quick heads-up and the charts. We're on it.

High-level: I'm opening an internal incident and looping infra. Initial read: a cache-coherency event looks possible — some customers saw a short window where prefix/KV cache entries were invalidated leading to a spiky backend load pattern and cold KV fetches. That would explain simultaneous p95/p99 regressions and a short rise in 5xxs as capacity momentarily strained.

Immediate asks for BlueWave: if you can share a sample request-id or timestamps for impacted requests (from trace-snippets.txt) that would help correlate. We're prioritizing a mitigation (fallback to warmed model variant / temporary routing to Dedicated pool) while we stabilize the cache.

I'll send updates in this thread every 30 minutes or on significant changes.

— Marissa Cole
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:38:45 +0000
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on Hosted API

Folks — escalating to infra + SRE. Quick summary: BlueWave reports coordinated p95/p99 regression in Hosted with a burst in throughput. My read from preliminary logs: at 15:14:xx UTC we observed a short-lived global invalidation signal for prefix KV caches originating from a control-plane config roll. The invalidation TTL was set incorrectly for a subset of routes; many active endpoints were forced to rehydrate caches simultaneously.

Immediate mitigation options (pick one):
- Roll back the config that triggered global invalidations (fastest).
- Apply staged rewarm: selectively rewarp heavy-hit prefixes into local cache for BlueWave routes (30–45m).
- Route BlueWave traffic to a warmed Dedicated pool / standby model to remove dependency on the shared prefix cache (requires ops approval).

I'll take the rollback unless legal/ops pushback. Sean: can you validate whether rollback triggers anything downstream (billing/telemetry)? Stephanie: please prepare a canary routing plan if rollback is risky. Aditya: flagging for exec awareness — we may need credits/compensation if SLA thresholds are breached.

Jonas Weber
VP, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: URGENT: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on Hosted API

Confirmed: rollback queued and ready. Audit shows the control-plane change (ID cfg-20270503-07) unintentionally flipped 'cache_invalidation=global' for tag 'customer:shared-prefix' for ~2 min during rollout. That produced a stampede of KV misses for heavily sharded prefixes.

Rollback impact: near-zero functional change, telemetry for the config will go back to previous state. Side-effects: shortened metric discontinuities but should stop further invalidations. I recommend rollback now + add short-term routing for BlueWave to warmed pool for 60 minutes while we monitor p95/p99.

Attached: config-audit.csv with the exact change window and affected routes. I'll start the rollback at 16:08 UTC unless someone objects.

— Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: config-audit.csv

Subject: Re: URGENT: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on Hosted API — mitigation and next steps

Alice — quick update and plan of record: thanks for your patience.

What happened (TL;DR): a control-plane rollout inadvertently triggered a global prefix/KV cache invalidation for shared prefixes. That caused a short window where many prefixes rehydrated simultaneously, temporarily spiking backend tokenization and model warm-up costs. Result: p95/p99 regressions and a small increase in 5xxs for ~18 minutes.

What we did:
- SRE rolled back cfg-20270503-07 at 16:09 UTC to restore previous cache-invalidation semantics.
- We applied selective routing: BlueWave traffic was routed to a warmed Dedicated pool for 60 minutes to avoid additional cold misses.
- Telemetry: continuous p95/p99 tracking with auto-alerting thresholds tightened.
- Postmortem items: config rollout guardrails (feature-flag + dry-run), targeted rewarm routines for heavy prefixes, and a short-term SLA remediation credit proposal.

Current status: metrics have returned to baseline in both regions; p95 and p99 are within normal bounds as of 19:40 UTC. We've attached traces and the config audit for your review.

Next steps:
1) We will share the postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow with actions and timelines.
2) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min technical sync to go over root cause and prevention steps.
3) Our Customer Ops lead will follow up re: SLA remediation.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We take incidents like this seriously and will incorporate learnings into our rollout playbook.

— Marissa Cole
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
